items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: I noticed some interesting titles in your work. “A Line for Dr. Cornel West”

ctx.x: development, that’s all in this type of music. And also there are so many things that we can learn about it because it’s intergenerational. You know I could go and play with 15- year-olds. I played with a young tenor player last night named Emilio Modeste. I mean he’s the spitting image of — like I thought I was playing next to Wayne Shorter and he’s probably half my age. You know and then I played with Sharon Jones, the great singer that’s in her seventies. And so I think that aspect of it, the social aspect and…

I was going to ask you about that because I noticed some interesting titles in your work. “A Line for Dr. Cornel West” and even an inspiration for the Sudoku Suite. Do you — I’m not sure how to ask this — do you look for inspiration or does it arrive somehow and you take note of it.

Yeah, that’s a heavy question. You know I’ve gone through periods where I’ll have several months where I’ll just go and go to a museum, like I went to the Gardner Museum and I just noticed the empty frames. And I said to myself what does that mean? And then I found out what those empty frames in the museum meant, it was symbolism hoping for those stolen pieces of artwork to come back. And so then I went online and I found the actual pieces of artwork and I just stared at them and read about the history of them…
